Wooden boxes, crates and chests, and metal boxes and chests. Ones that were made lockable can be locked and trapped. Each holds up to 125 items and 400 stones. A wooden box weighs 4 stones, a small or medium crate 2, a large crate 1 and a wooden chest 2.
# Locks

A box a Carpenter makes may be lockable: when it is finished the game checks your Tinkering skill (a sure thing from Tinkering 15), and if that is enough the box is lockable and its key is inside. Double-click the key and click the box to lock or unlock it. A locked box cannot be opened or filled. Lockpicks open it if your Lockpicking is high enough. The Magic Lock spell can lock a box that was made lockable; then lockpicks cannot open it, only its key or the Unlock spell. A box that was not made lockable cannot be locked at all.
# Traps

The Magic Trap spell, or a Tinker (Traps in the Tinkering menu, keyed boxes only), can trap a box. A Tinker's trap sleeps until the box is locked, then hurts whoever picks the lock. Remove Trap disarms a trap and needs Lockpicking and Detect Hidden of at least 50.
# Where to get them

A Carpenter makes a wooden box from 10 logs (Carpentry 21 to 46), a small crate from 8 (10 to 35), a medium crate from 15 (31 to 56), a large crate from 18 (47.3 to 72.3) and a wooden chest from 20 (73.6 to 98.6). Provisioners sell a wooden box for about 14 gold; it has no key and no lock.

items.title: Barrel and keg
paragraphs: # What they are
Casks that hold goods. A barrel weighs 25 stones and a keg 15. Each holds up to 125 items and 400 stones.
# Where to get them

A Carpenter builds a keg from 3 barrel staves, a barrel hoops and a barrel lid (Carpentry 57.8 to 82.8). The staves (5 logs each, Carpentry 0 to 25) and the lid (4 logs, Carpentry 11 to 36) are Carpenter's work; the hoops (5 iron ingots) are a Tinker's. A Tinker can turn a keg into a potion keg: read the Potion keg topic. Barrels are found as decoration, mostly in dungeons.

items.title: Armoire, bookcase
paragraphs: # What they are

Furniture that holds things. A piece fixed in place in a shop, street or dungeon (one you cannot pick up) cannot be filled: the game tells you it is not your container. One you carry in your pack, or have locked down in your own house, can be.
# Where to get them

A Carpenter builds an empty bookcase from 25 logs (Carpentry 31.5 to 56.5), an armoire or a fancy armoire from 35 logs each (Carpentry 84.2 to 109.2). Full bookcases, drawers and fancy drawers are only found as decoration.

items.title: Keys
paragraphs: # What it is
A key opens one lock and no other: every lockable box, chest or door has its own number, and a key carries a number too. A key weighs 1 stone. A blank key has no number yet.
# How to use it

Keep it in your pack, double-click it, then click the box or door (within 3 tiles). If the numbers match, it locks what is unlocked and unlocks what is locked. To name a key, double-click it and click the key itself. A blank key asks which key to copy: copying uses your Tinkering skill and can fail, with a 1 in 10 chance of ruining the blank.
# Where to get one
Provisioners sell blank keys for about 2 gold. A Tinker makes a blank from 3 iron ingots (Tinkering 20 to 70). A lockable box a Carpenter made for you has its key inside it.

items.title: Key ring
paragraphs: # What it is
A ring that holds up to 20 keys in one item that weighs 1 stone. Blank keys do not go on it.
# How to use it

Drag a key onto the ring while the ring is in your pack. Double-click the ring, then click a box or door: it tries each key until one fits, and tells you if you have none for it. Click the ring itself to take all the keys off again.
# Where to get it
No shopkeeper in this world sells key rings. A Tinker makes one from 2 iron ingots (Tinkering 10 to 60).

items.title: Dye tubs and dyes
paragraphs: # What they are
An ordinary dye tub paints things; the dyes set the color of the tub. A tub weighs 10 stones and a set of dyes 3.
# How to use them

First set the color: double-click the dyes and click the tub, then pick a color from the chart. Then double-click the tub and click what to paint. You and the tub must be within 1 tile of each other and of the thing. You can paint clothing, bags and backpacks, bandages, cloth, wool, cotton, yarn and thread, but not clothes you are wearing.
# Where to get them
Tailors and Weavers sell dye tubs and dyes for about 8 gold each.

items.title: Hair dye
paragraphs: # What it is
A dye for your hair and beard. It weighs 1 stone and is used up when you use it.
# How to use it
Keep it in your pack and double-click it, then choose a color from the chart. Your hair and your beard both take the color. You need some hair or a beard to use it.
# Where to get it
Alchemists sell hair dye for about 37 gold and Provisioners for about 60.

items.title: Dice and boards
paragraphs: # What they are
Dice and game boards for passing the time. Dice weigh 1 stone. A board weighs 5 stones and keeps its own pieces in it.
# How to use them
Double-click the dice, standing within 2 tiles: everyone nearby sees you roll two dice, each from 1 to 6. A board opens like a container; drag its pieces about on it to play.
# Where to get them
Provisioners, Innkeepers and Tavern Keepers sell dice, chessboards, checkerboards and backgammon boards for about 2 gold each.

items.title: Bedroll
paragraphs: # What it is
A rolled-up bed for camping. It weighs 5 stones.
# What it is for

Put it on the ground near you and double-click it to unroll it, and again to roll it up. Rolling it up in a secure camp opens a window: choose Continue within 10 seconds and you log out at once, safely, with the bedroll back in your pack. A camp is secure when you have stayed within 7 tiles of a burning campfire for 30 seconds; embers do not count. A bedroll in your pack does nothing until you put it down.

paragraphs.text: Every new character starts with a bedroll and some Kindling, kept loose in the pack and kept through death (a murderer loses them).

paragraphs: # Where to get it
Provisioners sell bedrolls for about 5 gold.

items.title: Table utensils
paragraphs: # What they are
Forks, knives and spoons for a table. They are decoration and do nothing when used. Each weighs 1 stone.
# Where to get them
No shopkeeper in this world sells them. A Tinker makes each from 1 iron ingot (Tinkering 0 to 50), left or right facing.

items.title: Books
paragraphs: # What they are

Books to read, and some to write in. Lore books (histories, journals and tales) are set out as decoration in Britain, a few other towns and some dungeons; you can read them but not change them. A blank book is writable: a red, brown or tan one has 20 pages and a blue one 40.
# How to use them

Double-click a book to open it. A blank book gets the title "a book" and your name as its author the first time you open it; then you can write in it. Click a book once to see its title, author and number of pages. A Scribe can copy a book into a blank one: use the Inscription skill, click the book to copy, then the blank book. It can fail; at Inscription 50 it never does.
# Where to get them
Scribes sell blank brown, tan and blue books for about 15 gold each, and Provisioners sell red, tan and blue ones for the same.

items.title: Spellbook
paragraphs: # What it is

The ordinary spellbook, the book of Magery. It holds the 64 spells of the eight circles, each one either in the book or not, and it weighs 3 stones. It is blessed, so it stays with you when you die. You can hold it in your hand as well as carry it.
# How to use it

Double-click it to open it; it must be in your pack (not inside a bag) or in your hand. A spell can be cast only if it is in a book you carry. To add a spell, drag a spell scroll onto the book (or open the scroll's menu, choose Add To Spellbook and click the book): one scroll of the stack is used up. A book that already has the spell refuses the scroll.
# Where to get it
Mages sell a spellbook for about 18 gold. One you buy is empty, so buy scrolls (Mages sell those of the first three circles) and drag them in.

items.title: Spell scrolls
paragraphs: # What they are
A scroll holds one spell to cast once. There are 64 spells in eight circles, and each is its own kind of scroll. Each scroll weighs 1 stone, and scrolls of one kind stack.
# How to use them

Double-click a scroll in your pack, then choose the target if the spell needs one. A scroll needs no reagents but costs the spell's mana, and it takes less Magery to cast a spell from a scroll than from a book. The scroll is used up when the spell goes off; if the cast fizzles you keep it. To keep the spell for good, drag the scroll onto your spellbook instead (or open the scroll's menu, choose Add To Spellbook and click the book).

paragraphs.text: A Recall scroll that would take a blue player into a Hot Zone from outside one asks first; if you cancel, nothing is used up. A gate, including one opened by Gate Travel, asks as you step in.

paragraphs: # Where to get them

Mages sell scrolls of the first three circles: about 12 gold for the first circle, 22 for the second and 32 for the third. Higher circles come as loot from monsters and in treasure chests. A character with the Inscription skill can make a scroll of any spell in their own spellbook, from a blank scroll, the spell's reagents and some mana.

items.title: Blank scroll
paragraphs: # What it is
A sheet ready to be written on. It weighs 1 stone, and blank scrolls stack.
# What it is for
Inscription turns one blank scroll into one spell scroll. A runebook takes 8 blank scrolls, a Recall scroll and a Gate Travel scroll.
# Where to get it
Scribes and Mages sell blank scrolls for about 5 gold each; a Mapmaker sells them for about 12.

items.title: Recall rune
paragraphs: # What it is
A stone that remembers a place. A new rune is blank ("unmarked"). It weighs 1 stone.
# How to use it

Cast the Mark spell (sixth circle) and click a blank rune in your pack: it remembers the spot where you stand. Double-click a marked rune to give it a name. Cast Recall (fourth circle) and click the rune, and you are taken to its place. Recall refuses you while you are a criminal, in a fight or overloaded, and some places refuse marking and recall.

paragraphs.text: If the trip would take a blue player into a Hot Zone from outside, the game asks first; cancelling costs nothing.

paragraphs: # Where to get it
Mages sell blank recall runes for about 15 gold.

items.title: Runebook
paragraphs: # What it is
A book of up to 16 recall runes, with a few charges for casting Recall from it. It weighs 3 stones, is blessed (it stays with you when you die) and can be held in your hand.
# How to use it

Drag marked runes onto it. Drag Recall scrolls onto it to charge it: each adds a charge, up to the book's limit. Double-click it to open it. In the open book, the button next to a rune's name recalls you to that place with one charge: no reagents and no Recall spell needed, though it still costs mana. A rune's own page also has Recall and Gate buttons, which cast those spells from your own spellbook instead, and Drop rune and Set default. Casting Recall and clicking the book takes you to its default place. After a trip the book needs 7 seconds to recover.
# Where to get it

A Scribe makes one by Inscription (45 to 95) from 8 blank scrolls, a Recall scroll and a Gate Travel scroll. Its charge limit is 7 to 10, higher with more Inscription skill and for exceptional quality.

items.title: Maps
paragraphs: # What they are
A blank map is an empty sheet. A Cartographer draws it into a local map, a city map, a sea chart or a world map. Each weighs 1 stone.
# How to use them

Double-click a drawn map, standing within 2 tiles, to open it. A local map, city map or sea chart shows the land around the place where it was drawn, and a map drawn with more Cartography skill shows a wider area. A world map is always centred on Britain and also grows with your skill. A blank map only tells you it is blank.
# How to make one

Use the Cartography skill (or double-click a mapmaker's pen) and choose a map; each takes one blank map. A local map needs Cartography 10 to 70, a city map 25 to 85, a sea chart 35 to 95 and a world map 39.5 to 99.5. Mapmakers sell blank maps for about 5 gold.

items.title: Bulk order deeds
paragraphs: # What it is

A Blacksmith's bulk order: a request for a number of one kind of armor or weapon. A small deed asks for 10, 15 or 20 of one item; a large deed asks for several different items. Some deeds demand exceptional quality or a certain metal.
# How to use it

Double-click the deed to read what it needs. Choose the button that combines the deed with the item requested, then click an item in your pack that fits. A large deed is filled by combining the small deeds that match its entries. When it is complete, drag it onto a Blacksmith to be paid in gold (a bank check when it is over 1,000) and fame, and sometimes an item.
# Where to get one

A Blacksmith offers an order to a character with some Blacksmithing skill: click the Blacksmith and choose Bulk Order Info, or you may be offered one after you sell him goods. You can be offered a new one every hour below Blacksmithing 50.1, every 2 hours from 50.1 and every 6 hours from 70.1; large deeds come only from 70.1.

items.title: A weapon
paragraphs: # What it is

A weapon. Equip it to fight with it. Each kind uses one combat skill (Swordsmanship, Fencing, Mace Fighting or Archery); with empty hands you fight with Wrestling. The help pages for swords, axes, maces, bows and the other common weapons say what each is for and where to get it. This page is what all weapons share.

paragraphs.text: Hover the pointer over any weapon to see its damage, speed, Strength needed, whether it takes one hand or two, and the skill it uses.

paragraphs: # Using it

You need at least the weapon's Strength requirement to equip it; if you do not, the game says You are not strong enough to equip that. A two-handed weapon cannot be used with a shield. A one-handed weapon can.

Each hit rolls between the weapon's lowest and highest damage. Tactics, Strength and Anatomy then change it, a worn weapon does less (down to half with no durability left), and the target's armor and shield take some away. A hit on another player does half damage. A swing takes 15000 / ((stamina + 100) x speed) seconds, which is 75 / speed at 100 stamina, so a higher speed swings faster. Your stamina can never be higher than your Dexterity. The Skill Guide ([SkillGuide) explains your weapon skill, Tactics and Anatomy in full.

paragraphs.text: New fighter help: when your swing time is worked out, a stamina below 60 counts as 60, and when your damage is worked out, a Tactics below 30 counts as 30.

paragraphs: # Durability and repair

About one hit in 25 costs a weapon a point of durability, and slimes and acid elementals cost a melee weapon a point on every hit. With none left it starts to lose its maximum, and when that is used up it breaks and is gone. Arms Lore tells you a weapon's condition and how hard it hits. A Blacksmith can repair the weapons a Blacksmith can forge, and the Pitchfork: choose Repair in the Blacksmith menu, near a forge and anvil, with the weapon in your backpack and no poison on it. A repair can lower its maximum a little.
# Magic and quality

Some weapons from monsters or treasure chests are magical, and read as unidentified until you use Item Identification on them. Accurate, surpassingly accurate, eminently accurate, exceedingly accurate and supremely accurate add 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 to your Tactics (to your Archery with a bow or crossbow). Ruin, might, force, power and vanquishing add 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 to each damage roll. Durable, substantial, massive, fortified and indestructible add 20%, 50%, 70%, 100% and 120% to durability. An exceptional weapon from a skilled maker does 20% more damage and has 20% more durability.
# Buying and selling

Shopkeepers pay about half of what they charge for ordinary weapons, plus 100 gold for each step of ruin or durability. They will not buy newbied gear such as your starting weapon, which you keep when you die (a murderer loses it).

items.title: Swords
paragraphs: # What they are
Swords are one-handed blades that use the Swordsmanship skill, so you can carry a shield with one. The Kryss is a Fencing weapon and has its own page.
# Good to know

Speed counts as much as damage: a Katana swings a good deal faster than a Longsword. Slimes and acid elementals scar a sword on every hit. Double-click a sword and click a corpse to carve it, or a tree to cut Kindling. With the Poisoning skill you can coat a sword with a poison potion: each hit then uses one of 12 to 18 charges and poisons about half the time.
A new Swordsmanship or Tactics character starts with a Katana. It is newbied: you keep it when you die (a murderer loses it) and shops will not buy it.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell them for about: Cutlass 24 gold, Thin longsword 27, Katana 33, Broadsword 35, Scimitar 36, Longsword 55, Viking sword 55. Only about one weaponsmith in three stocks swords, so a Blacksmith is the sure place. A Blacksmith forges all but the Thin longsword from iron ingots; the Blacksmithy page lists the skill and ingots each needs. Monsters also drop swords.

items.title: Dagger and kryss
paragraphs: # What they are
The Dagger and the Kryss are one-handed piercing blades that use the Fencing skill, not Swordsmanship. You can carry a shield with them.
# Good to know
Both swing fast. A new Fencing character starts with a Kryss. It is newbied: you keep it when you die (a murderer loses it) and shops will not buy it.

Double-click one and click a corpse to carve it, or a tree to cut Kindling. With the Poisoning skill you can coat either with a poison potion: each hit then uses one of 12 to 18 charges and poisons about half the time. See A weapon for how damage, speed and durability work.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell the Dagger for about 21 gold and the Kryss for 32. A Blacksmith forges both from iron ingots. The Dagger needs only 3 and is the first weapon you can try to forge, even at Blacksmithy 0, though it rarely works until the skill has grown a little.

items.title: Knives
paragraphs: # What they are

Small one-handed knives that use the Swordsmanship skill. They are poor weapons but handy tools: double-click one and click a corpse to carve it (meat, hides, feathers or wool, when the creature has any), or click a tree to cut Kindling.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell the Butcher knife for about 14 gold, the Cleaver for 15 and the Skinning knife for 14. A tinker makes all three from 2 or 3 iron ingots; a Blacksmith does not forge them. See A weapon for how damage, speed and durability work.

items.title: Spears and forks
paragraphs: # What they are
Spears and forks are piercing weapons that use the Fencing skill. The Spear, Short spear and Pitchfork are two-handed, so no shield; the War fork is one-handed.
# Good to know
The Short spear is the quick one. Only the one-handed War fork can be coated with poison (Poisoning skill). The Pitchfork is a farm tool and does the least damage.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell the Short spear for about 23 gold, the Spear for 31 and the Pitchfork for 19; weaponsmiths sell the War fork for 32. A Blacksmith forges the Short spear, Spear and War fork under Build Pole Arms; the Pitchfork cannot be forged.

items.title: Axes
paragraphs: # What they are
Axes hit hard and swing slowly. Six are two-handed and use the Swordsmanship skill. The War axe is the exception: it is one-handed, trains Mace Fighting and cannot chop wood.
# Good to know

For every axe but the War axe, each 5 points of Lumberjacking add 1% to its damage, and fighting with one slowly trains Lumberjacking. To chop a tree, equip the axe (the game will not chop with one that is only in your pack), double-click it and click the tree. Chopping does not wear an axe out; fighting does.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell them for about: Battle axe 26 gold, War axe 29, Executioner's axe 30, Two handed axe 32, Large battle axe 33, Axe 40, Double axe 52. A Blacksmith forges all seven from iron ingots under Build Axes; the Blacksmithy page lists the skill and ingots each needs. Monsters also drop axes.

items.title: Hatchet
paragraphs: # What it is
The lumberjack's tool, and a light two-handed axe. In a fight it uses the Swordsmanship skill.
# What it is for
Equip it, double-click it and click a tree to chop logs; the game will not chop with a hatchet that is only in your pack. Chopping does not wear it out.

paragraphs.text: Once you start on a tree you keep chopping it until the wood runs out or you do something else, such as walk, fight, cast a spell or use another skill.

paragraphs: # Where to get it

Weaponsmiths sell hatchets for about 25 to 27 gold. A tinker can make one from 4 iron ingots (Tinkering 30 and up). A new Lumberjacking character starts with one. Every axe on the Axes page except the War axe chops too.

items.title: Pickaxes
paragraphs: # What they are
The miner's tool, and a weak one-handed axe in a fight (Swordsmanship skill).
# What it is for

Double-click it and click a mountainside or cave floor to dig ore. You cannot dig while riding. Each successful dig uses one of its uses (a new pickaxe has 50, more if it was made exceptional); when they are gone the pickaxe is worn out and destroyed.

paragraphs.text: Once you start on a spot you keep digging it until the ore runs out or you do something else, such as walk, fight, cast a spell or use another skill.

paragraphs: # Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell pickaxes for about 22 gold, and the Miner and the Tinker for about 25. A tinker can make one from 4 iron ingots (Tinkering 40 and up). Some gargoyles carry a gargoyle's pickaxe, which has 101 to 125 uses.

items.title: Maces and clubs
paragraphs: # What they are

Clubs, maces and hammers use the Mace Fighting skill. Every hit also takes 3 to 5 points of stamina from the target, which slows its swings. All are one-handed, so you can carry a shield, except the War hammer.
# Good to know

They are heavy, so watch your load. A new Mace Fighting character starts with a Club. It is newbied: you keep it when you die (a murderer loses it) and shops will not buy it. See A weapon for how damage, speed and durability work.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell them for about: Club 16 gold, Maul 21, War hammer 25, Hammer pick 26, Mace 28, War mace 31. A Blacksmith forges all but the Club from iron ingots under Build Bludgeoning Weapons. Monsters also drop them.

items.title: Staves
paragraphs: # What they are
Staves are two-handed, so no shield, and use the Mace Fighting skill. Every hit also takes 3 to 5 points of stamina from the target.
# Good to know
The Quarter staff is the quick one. See A weapon for how damage, speed and durability work.
# Where to get them

Weaponsmiths, blacksmiths and carpenters sell them for about: Gnarled staff 16 gold, Quarter staff 19, Black staff 22. A carpenter can make the Quarter staff and the Gnarled staff from logs, but only at high Carpentry skill (about 74 and about 79); the Black staff cannot be made.

items.title: Shepherd's crook
paragraphs: # What it is
The herder's tool, and a light two-handed staff. In a fight it uses the Mace Fighting skill, and each hit takes 3 to 5 points of stamina from the target.
# What it is for
Double-click it, click an animal that is wild but could be tamed, then click where you want it to go. Whether it goes depends on your Herding skill; a pet already looks tame and will not be herded.
# Where to get it

Weaponsmiths, blacksmiths and carpenters sell it for about 20 gold. A carpenter can make one at high Carpentry skill (about 79). A new character who starts with Herding, Animal Lore or Animal Taming carries one.

items.title: Pole arms
paragraphs: # What they are
The Bardiche and the Halberd are two-handed pole arms that use the Swordsmanship skill. Their damage ranges are the biggest of the melee weapons, and they swing slowly.
# Good to know
A pole arm will chop trees like an axe when it is equipped, but each successful chop uses up one of its 150 uses and the last one destroys it, so keep a hatchet for wood.
# Where to get them
Blacksmiths sell the Halberd for about 42 gold and the Bardiche for 60. A Blacksmith forges both from iron ingots under Build Pole Arms. Monsters also drop them.

items.title: Bow
paragraphs: # What it is

A two-handed ranged weapon that shoots arrows up to 10 tiles and uses the Archery skill. Being two-handed, it cannot be used with a shield. A Juka bow, which Juka lords carry, is a Bow that needs 80 Strength and 80 Dexterity.
# Shooting

Each shot uses one arrow from your backpack, hit or miss (see Arrows and bolts); with none left the bow simply stops shooting. You need a clear line to the target within 10 tiles, and you must be standing still: after your last step there is a pause before you can shoot, 1 second at 25 Dexterity or less, shorter as Dexterity rises, and 0.5 second at 100. See A weapon for how damage and speed work.
# Where to get it

Blacksmiths sell bows for about 35 gold and bowyers for 40. A character with Bowcraft/Fletching can make one from 7 logs (skill 30 and up). A new Archery character starts with a Bow, which is newbied: you keep it when you die (a murderer loses it) and shops will not buy it.

items.title: Crossbows
paragraphs: # What they are
Two-handed ranged weapons that shoot bolts, not arrows, and use the Archery skill. Being two-handed, they cannot be used with a shield. Both reach 8 tiles, less than a bow, and shoot slowly.
# Shooting

Each shot uses one bolt from your backpack, hit or miss (see Arrows and bolts); with none left the weapon simply stops shooting. You need a clear line to the target within 8 tiles, and you must be standing still: after your last step there is a pause before you can shoot, 1 second at 25 Dexterity or less, shorter as Dexterity rises, and 0.5 second at 100.
# Where to get them

Blacksmiths sell the Crossbow for about 46 gold and the Heavy crossbow for 55; bowyers sell both for 55. With Bowcraft/Fletching you can make a Crossbow from 7 logs (skill 60 and up) and a Heavy crossbow from 10 logs (skill 80 and up).

items.title: Arrows and bolts
paragraphs: # What they are

Arrows are for bows; bolts are for crossbows and heavy crossbows. A shot uses one up, hit or miss, and a bow or crossbow with none in your backpack does not shoot. Each weighs a tenth of a stone, so 100 weigh 10 stones.
# Getting them back

Some are not lost. About 4 misses in 10 leave the arrow or bolt on the ground near the target. About 4 hits in 10 on an animal or a monster put it in the creature's pack, if it has one, so check its corpse. Shots at other players and at human enemies are not saved when they hit.

paragraphs.text: A new character who starts with Archery is given 100 arrows.

paragraphs: # Where to get them

Provisioners sell arrows for about 2 gold and bolts for 5; bowyers sell arrows for 2 and bolts for 3. A provisioner starts with only 20 of each and a bowyer with 30 to 89. You can also make your own with Bowcraft/Fletching from shafts and feathers (skill 0 and up).

items.title: Wands
paragraphs: # What they are

A wand holds charges of one magical effect. The kinds you can find are clumsiness, feeblemindedness, weakness, mana draining, magic arrow, harming, fireball, lightning, healing, greater healing and identification. A wand with charges reads as unidentified until you use Item Identification on it.
# How to use one

Equip the wand, double-click it and choose a target. It costs no mana and no reagents, never fizzles, has no casting delay and spends one charge. Wait about 4 seconds between uses (an identification wand has no wait). When the charges are gone the game tells you. In a fight a wand, with charges or without, is only a weak one-handed club (Mace Fighting, damage 2 to 6).
# Where to get them
Shops do not sell wands. They turn up in the better locked treasure chests in dungeons.

items.title: Wear and repair
paragraphs: # What it is

Weapons, armor and shields wear out. Each has a durability: how much it has left now, and the most it can ever hold. A new ordinary piece starts full. A successful use of Arms Lore tells you how worn a piece is.

paragraphs.text: On the combat bar a thin gauge beside the weapon and shield slots, and beside each piece in the strip that opens when you hold a slot, shows it at a glance: all green when new, with red filling from the top as it wears out.
You are told once when a piece you wear or wield drops to about a quarter of its durability.

paragraphs: # How it wears
A weapon loses a point of durability on about one hit in 25 that you land with it. Against slimes and acid elementals a melee weapon loses a point on every hit.

Armor wears when you are hit. A blow that lands on a piece has a 1 in 4 chance of wearing it, by 1 point or by none. A bashing weapon such as a mace wears it faster: by half of what the piece soaked up, and at least 1.
A shield wears only when it blocks a blow, and then only 1 time in 4, by 1 point or by none.
# When it runs out
A worn piece does less. A weapon's damage and an armor piece's rating shrink as the durability falls, down to half of their full value at 0.
At 0 the wear starts to lower the most the piece can hold instead, and you are told "Your equipment is severely damaged." A piece whose maximum is used up is destroyed and is gone.
# Repair

Only a Blacksmith can repair, and only what a Blacksmith can make: metal armor, helmets, every shield but the plain wooden shield, the weapons a Blacksmith forges, and the Pitchfork. Leather, studded leather and bone armor and clothing cannot be repaired by anyone: when they wear out you buy or make new ones.

Stand near an anvil and a forge with the piece in your backpack (not worn), use a smith's hammer or tongs, choose Repair in the Blacksmith menu and then the piece. A weapon with poison on it cannot be repaired.
A repair is a Blacksmithing check, and it gets harder the more worn the piece is, so repair early: a piece worn right down is hard even for a Grandmaster. On success the piece is full again.

A repair also costs the piece some of its maximum, though not every time. The chance is 40 in 100, plus 1 for each point of durability it is missing, minus 1 for each 10 points of your Blacksmithing. When it happens the maximum falls by 3 below Blacksmithing 70, by 2 from 70, and by 1 from 90. A piece whose maximum is no more than that refuses: "That item has been repaired many times, and will break if repairs are attempted again."
# Good to know

An exceptional piece from a skilled maker has 20 percent more durability, and a magical piece called durable, substantial, massive, fortified or indestructible has 20, 50, 70, 100 or 120 percent more. Magical pieces read as unidentified until Item Identification reveals them.
